source.title: A Perceptual Inference Mechanism for Hallucinations Linked to Striatal Dopamine

confidence_rationale: This is the strongest available evidence for the BEHAVIOURAL half of MECH-043's CONFIRMING condition -- that raising a dopamine-dependent gain on expectations produces a measurable shift in a hallucination-like dependent variable. The causal chain is unusually complete for a human study: the perceptual bias was pharmacologically INDUCED by amphetamine (not merely correlated), the induced bias correlated strongly with directly measured striatal dopamine release (PET displacement), and the bias tracked hallucination severity in unmedicated patients. Source quality is high (molecular imaging plus pharmacological manipulation plus a purpose-built psychophysical task, top-tier venue, Daw/Horga/Abi-Dargham). Mapping fidelity is the limiting factor and is where confidence is docked: the quantity measured is gain on PRIOR EXPECTATIONS under uncertainty, which in a precision-weighting scheme is the complement of precision on the sensory prediction error rather than that precision itself. REE's current_precision sits on the error side of that balance, so the mapping is one inversion away from literal. Sample sizes are modest by pharmacological-imaging standards.
failure_signatures: The dopamine-dependent quantity manipulated here is gain on PRIOR EXPECTATIONS, not precision on the unsigned prediction error. If REE raises current_precision (confidence in its own error estimate) and expects a hallucination-like shift on the strength of this paper, the inference runs through an assumed reciprocity between prior weight and error precision that this study does not itself establish.

The effect was anchored to the DORSAL ANTERIOR CINGULATE (cortical volume of dACC related to the bias) and to associative striatum. A REE ablation that isolates the E3 selector's precision channel from the dACC affective-PE weighting may find the effect does not survive the isolation, which would meet MECH-043 falsifier (iii).

Amphetamine is a non-selective monoamine releaser: it raises noradrenaline and serotonin alongside dopamine. Attribution to dopamine rests on the correlation with PET-measured striatal displacement, not on pharmacological selectivity, so this does not by itself exclude MECH-043 falsifier (iv) (a shared, non-dopamine-specific precision-scale parameter).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Hallucination severity in unmedicated patients with schizophrenia correlates with a perceptual bias reflecting disproportionate gain on prior expectations under uncertainty, measured with a task probing illusory changes in the perceived duration of auditory stimuli. The same bias can be pharmacologically induced in healthy individuals by amphetamine, is strongly correlated with amphetamine-induced striatal dopamine release measured by PET, and is related to cortical volume of the dorsal anterior cingulate, a region involved in tracking environmental uncertainty. The authors conclude that a dopamine-dependent gain-control process over prior expectations confers vulnerability to hallucinations in hyper-dopaminergic states.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-043's CONFIRMING condition has two halves: a mechanistic half (the precision term is unsigned, live-wired, and influences commitment) and a behavioural half (misallocation of this channel produces a measurable shift in a hallucination-like DV). Haarsma et al. 2021 supply the mechanistic half; this paper is the best available evidence for the behavioural half, and it is causal rather than correlational -- amphetamine INDUCED the bias, and the size of the induction tracked directly measured striatal dopamine release. For REE this is the design template as much as the evidence: it shows what a hallucination-like DV can concretely look like (a signed perceptual displacement toward the prior, measured under parametrically varied uncertainty) and that a gain-control parameter is the right knob to sweep. The dACC finding is a second, narrower point of contact: REE feeds current_precision into dACC affective-PE weighting as well as the E3 commitment gate, and this paper independently implicates dACC in tracking the uncertainty that the gain is applied under.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The central inversion must be stated plainly. In a precision-weighting scheme, excessive weight on priors and excessive precision on sensory prediction errors are OPPOSITE dispositions -- the first ignores incoming evidence, the second over-attends to it. This paper manipulates the prior side; REE's current_precision = 1/(running_variance + eps) sits on the error side. The mapping to MECH-043 therefore runs through an assumed reciprocity (low precision on the error term equals high relative weight on the prior), which is true of an idealised Bayesian balance but is NOT guaranteed in REE's implementation, where running_variance is a self-estimated EMA rather than a normalised term in a two-sided inference. The practical consequence is directional: this paper predicts a hallucination-like shift when REE's precision channel is DOWN-weighted or mis-scaled relative to the prior, and a REE sweep that only raises precision may look for the effect in the wrong direction. Two further limits: amphetamine is not dopamine-selective (attribution rests on the PET correlation), and the sample sizes are modest for pharmacological imaging.
mapping.source_context: Unmedicated patients with schizophrenia varying in hallucination severity plus healthy individuals. Methods: PET molecular imaging of striatal dopamine release under an amphetamine challenge, structural MRI, and a purpose-built auditory task measuring illusory changes in perceived stimulus duration under parametrically varied uncertainty. Human, auditory modality, within-subject pharmacological challenge.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: causal pharmacological induction plus direct molecular measurement of the putative mediator plus a clinical gradient, which is a rare combination; docked for modest N and for amphetamine's lack of monoamine selectivity. Mapping fidelity is the binding constraint at 0.68 -- the paper's quantity is prior-weight gain, REE's is error precision, and these are complementary rather than identical. Transfer risk elevated accordingly: the direction of a predicted REE effect depends on a reciprocity assumption that has not been verified in REE's own implementation.
